name: Iqmaxxing

lead: Iqmaxxing is looksmax-forum shorthand for working to raise intelligence and mental performance. Forum guides cover lifestyle habits, skill-building, supplements and, in some threads, prescription or research compounds.

The link to looks is indirect: members tie it to confidence, conversation, career and the wider "ascension" project, and treat it as one more area to optimize alongside the face and body. Researchers describe IQ as substantially heritable and give mixed or limited support for most cognitive enhancers in healthy people.

paras: Guides on looksmax.org combine sleep, training and diet habits, learning and skill practice, and supplement lists, sometimes with community rating tables of compounds. Forum members debate which methods affect underlying IQ versus performance on a given day.

Over-the-counter supplements can be mislabeled, and the American Medical Association discouraged prescribing nootropics to healthy people in 2016. Prescription and research compounds discussed in some threads have side effects and legal restrictions and should be discussed with a clinician.

angle.text: Members frame a sharper mind as part of the complete package of how a person comes across. The effect on physical appearance is not direct; the link is through confidence, communication and skill.

lead: Iqmaxxing, short for IQ maxxing, is a term used on looksmaxxing forums for efforts to raise intelligence and cognitive performance.[1] Threads under the term include general guides, skill-building and learning advice, supplement rankings and discussions of prescription and research compounds.[2][3][4]

Its place in a looks-focused community is as part of whole-person self-improvement: members connect a sharper mind to confidence, social presentation and career, alongside physical changes. The community disagrees internally about how much IQ can be changed; one widely read rebuttal thread argues that raw IQ cannot be boosted by hacks and that gains come from knowledge and skill, while other threads present supplement stacks.[5][6]

paras: Forum guides range from beginner overviews to long compound libraries with mechanisms and pros and cons.[2][4][7] Some threads pair cognitive work with skill acquisition, using the term skillmaxxing for that side.[8]

One thread, written as a response to a long "Book of Intelligence" post, takes the position that artificially raising raw IQ is not possible and that performance can be improved by learning and efficient use of the brain.[5] Others present supplement and compound approaches.[3][4] Participants also ask how to learn about substances such as anabolic steroids, in threads where other members urge checking information carefully.[9]

The APA report summarized on Wikipedia puts heritability of IQ at about 0.45 in children and about 0.75 in late adolescents and adults, and describes nutrition, disease burden and education as environmental influences.[10] A 2008 study reported transfer of fluid-intelligence gains from working-memory training, though it is unclear whether such gains last or generalize.[10]

Wikipedia's nootropic article says low doses of some stimulants show benefits in healthy people in reviews, evidence is weak or mixed for racetams and many herbs, and vitamins and omega-3s do not enhance cognition in people without a deficiency. It reports that the AMA discouraged prescribing nootropics to healthy people in 2016 and that the FDA and FTC warned about fraudulent supplement marketing in 2019.[11]
No studies found on iqmaxxing itself. Studies of individual interventions, such as working-memory training and stimulant use in healthy adults, are discussed in the general references above.[10][11]

lore.intro: Iqmaxxing threads are mixed between supplement and drug enthusiasm and skepticism that IQ can be raised.[3][5]
